mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy cycle, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for this signal falls below 0.03 over any 2-year window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the federal funds rate above 2% triggers a tightening cycle, raising borrowing costs and dampening equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite FEDFUNDS crossing above 2%, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in tightening periods.

mechanism_narrative: Strong growth in consumer demand (GDPC1) coupled with constrained supply (INDPRO) creates upward pressure on prices and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction does not predict positive returns in >60% of instances where GDPC1 ↑ and INDPRO ↓ occur, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising labor demand (PAYEMS) combined with monetary easing (FEDFUNDS decline) creates a dual catalyst for economic growth, enhancing corporate profits and equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The combined effect of PAYEMS ↑ and FEDFUNDS ↓ does not consistently predict positive returns, or the Rank IC remains above 0.03 over any 2-year period.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected surge in unemployment (UNRATE) above 3.5% signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite UNRATE crossing above 3.5%, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in such periods.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a decline in the federal funds rate amplifies its positive impact on equity valuations by reducing discount rates, leading to stronger positive S&P 500 forward returns compared to other regimes over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The impact of FEDFUNDS decline on returns is not significantly stronger than in other regimes over 60 days, or the 60-day forward returns are not higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Strong growth in both consumer spending (GDPC1) and housing demand (HOUST) signals robust economic momentum, boosting corporate earnings and equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The combined effect of GDPC1 and HOUST increases does not predict positive returns in >80% of instances, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 1-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a post-shock recovery phase, a decline in the federal funds rate alongside rising industrial production (INDPRO) signals policy accommodation and improving supply chains, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction does not consistently predict positive returns in post-shock periods, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) over 60 days.
